summary: Candidate = head 4ccfb16 (w21 ink print, restored by f9956d5) + the uncommitted 10_mono.js change: the door-3 bar upper unit rebuilt as the in-service galley face (serviceFace), counter barTop #0e0e0f r0.4, carcass barFace #3a3835, blind rolled up into a black head, tumblers and bottle shelf removed, water bottles in the right bay, green LED on the brewer bay. Paired with omaat_j32, the bar now has no structural mismatch. Control panel over two ovens, landscape monitor over two open bays (brewer left, bottles right), and a tall glass-door cabinet with round latch, caution plate and cream tag are all in the right order and at the right heights. Measured tone distribution of the whole upper face: photo (165-1010,130-760) p10/50/90 10/53/165; after q11 (190-555,140-345) 11/54/180, m05 3/56/194; before q11 4/30/186. Element values match: ovens L136-138 vs photo L140, cabinet stile L51 vs L46, carcass beside the monitor L18 vs L24. Counter q11 p50 79 -> 53, m05 p50 27, photo 31-34. The bar detail rises from 8.6 to 8.7. It is held below 8.8 by three things. The glass-door cabinet still reads as open shelving (no glass cue; the same shared code as the welcome galley). The control panel is a flat plate (L139 uniform) where the photo has a dark recessed switch field. The door-2 welcome galley is now an identical copy of the same face, 16 m forward. q01/q19/q13 are pixel-identical (0 changed px), so their scores carry. The ink print is back to w21 (my w21a 8.6), so the w22a gains and losses on it are both gone. Area score holds at 8.7. There is no high issue.
lighting_note: Not scored. The recessed bays render crushed: right bay interior L3 against photo L11, and the dark bay floor/shelf edges vanish. The counter in q11 reads mid-grey (p50 53, p90 100) from the white canopy's reflection; the photo counter is p50 31 with long bright streaks. The q11 ash doors (L172, B/R 0.79) sit between omaat_j32 (L130-135, very warm camera white balance) and trafficnews (L161, B/R 0.85), so they need no change.

calibration.issue: Integration L13 (medium): door-3 bar follows ANA's 2019 render; the in-service face (omaat_j32) differs. Back face flat L30, counter p50 78 vs 37.
calibration.evidence: No structural mismatch with omaat_j32 remains (ovens + control panel left, monitor over brewer / open bay, glass-door cabinet right, no blind / tumblers / bottle shelf). L13 target 'back face L50-70, not flat L30': q11 face p50 30 -> 54 (p10/p90 11/180 vs photo 10/165), m05 30 -> 56. Counter: q11 (130-560,345-380) p50 79 -> 53, m05 p50 27; photo 31-34. The fixer deviated from the L13 spec in three places: counter r0.4, not 0.15; the nosing was already present and is unchanged; the cabinet uses the shared no-pane treatment, not 0.6-transmission glass. The result meets the targets.

calibration.evidence: q11 ash L172 B/R 0.79. omaat_j32 ash L130-135 B/R 0.58-0.61 (strong warm camera white balance); trafficnews_2019 ash L161 B/R 0.85. The model sits inside the spread of the real photos, so this is exposure, not material.

calibration.status: tumbler glints: moot (tumblers removed). Others not fixed.
calibration.evidence: q11 after: no tumblers. The nosing is unchanged. The cabinet still has no glass cue, now in both the welcome galley and the bar. The lavs, q01 and q19 are unchanged.

calibration.issue: Location evidence: is omaat_j32 the door-3 bar?
calibration.evidence: For: (1) OMAAT's text places 'a small snack bar between the middle and rear business class cabins', which is door 3 (REFERENCE777: door-3 galley becomes the self-service bar). (2) omaat_j32 shows a passenger-side counter with beige ash doors and the aluminium nosing in the foreground. That is the bar's lower half, as in trafficnews_2019, not a working galley with cart bays. (3) omaat_j30_snacks shows self-service snacks and amenities laid out on that counter in front of the same ovens and green-LED brewers. (4) knav_31 shows the same face with water bottles and a lav door to the right; door-3 lavs adjoin the bar. Caveat: trafficnews_2019 corroborates the counter, ash doors, black glossy top, a left roller blind and a monitor right of it, but not the new proportions. Its blind-down left bay is about 1.3x the monitor width, measured as width over local carcass height (145/245 px vs 90/190 px). In omaat_j32 the oven column is about 0.65x the monitor (170/400 vs 320/480). Its right column is a narrow lit strip and there is a wine shelf under the monitor. Both of those match the old render layout (narrow fridge, bottle shelf). So the 2019 preview face may have differed, or been re-fitted, from the 2020 in-service face. Following the in-service 2020 photo is the right call under the brief, since real in-flight photos win for geometry. The claim that trafficnews shows 'the same carcass' is only partly true.

issues.title: Glass-door cabinet reads as open shelving (no glass cue), now on both the bar and the welcome galley
issues.evidence: m05 pane (655-780,180-400) p10/50/90 38/42/67, B/R 0.95, against omaat_j32 pane (760-900,200-680) 31/60/83. In the photo the pane is a uniform smoked field with soft reflections; the contents are barely legible and the stile is wide (cabinet stile 700-725 is ~12 % of the cabinet width). In m05 / q11 the grey boxes and three crisp shelf lines read as an open shelf unit, and the right stile is thin (~2 %).
issues.fix: 10_mono.js serviceFace. Add one smoked pane quad on the glass plane, gQuad(cW-0.1, 0.66) at V(c0, 1.43, o+0.0865), material { c: '#2e2c2b', r: 0.08, a: 0.55 } or the glass material at 0.6 transmission. Alternatively, darken the interior shelves '#6a6766' -> '#4a4847' and the boxes by about 0.75x. Widen both stiles 0.05 -> 0.07 m. Check that it does not read as a panelled door; w9-w10a found an opaque pane did.

issues.title: Control panel is a flat bright plate
issues.evidence: m05 control panel (175-300,145-200) L139, p10-p90 135-142. omaat_j32 control panel (175-290,190-290) p10/50/90 45/96/156: a light frame around a dark recessed field with toggles, orange/red lamps and a small display.

issues.title: Door-2 welcome galley and door-3 bar are now identical faces
issues.evidence: serviceFace is called by both buildWelcomeGalley and buildBar. The welcome galley was built from omaat_room_32 (= omaat_j32), which is now assigned to door 3. Its remaining door-2 evidence is lalf_133/134 (door 2L, not in ref/web now). knav_31 is named 'entrance' and could be door 2 rather than door 3.
issues.fix: No geometry change unless lalf_134 contradicts it. Record in REFERENCE777.md which photos support each copy (door 3: omaat_j32, j30_snacks; door 2: lalf_134, and knav_31 if it is door 2). If lalf_134 shows a different insert layout at door 2, give serviceFace an option flag.

issues.evidence: m05 right bay interior (470-600,320-350) L3, against omaat_j32 bay (490-680,480-650) L11, where the bay floor and shelf edge read as grey lines (L30-45). Mostly lighting (AO in a deep recess).
issues.fix: serviceFace bay back { c: '#1d1c19' } -> '#2a2925', and add a 10 mm alu edge strip at each bay floor front, gBox(0.43, 0.01, 0.01) at y 1.035 and o+0.095 in MONMAT.aluDark. Otherwise this is a lighting note.

issues.title: Carried: w21 ink-print lows (blobby strata, soft edges) and the w18-w20 lows
issues.evidence: The w21 print was restored (f9956d5); q01/q19 are unchanged.
issues.fix: As in monuments_w21a, but this time thin the strata without raising coverage. Keep the dark fraction at 35-45 % (w22b B).

questions: Is lalf_134 (door 2L) still available? It should confirm that the door-2 welcome galley really carries the same oven / monitor / glass-cabinet face, now that omaat_j32 is assigned to the door-3 bar.
knav_31 is named 'entrance'. Is it the door-2 boarding view or the door-3 bar? Either way it supports the face, but it decides whether both monuments have in-service evidence.

trafficnews_2019 (press preview) shows a wider blind bay, a narrow lit column and a wine shelf, which is closer to the old render than to omaat_j32. Do we accept that the in-service 2020 face supersedes the 2019 preview? I think yes.
